title: Release cannot open a pull request when the workspace branch IS the remote's default branch (UnAI: master → master)
description:
Measured live on UnAI 2026-09-18 (goal "Uai — Personal AI Chief of Staff", build 4bc2ef7b + a36854f6).

The lander commits every accepted node onto the workspace branch (`[lander] COMMITTED (361909707c on master, 46 files)`), the publisher's candidate is `symbolic-ref HEAD` of that workspace (`apps/daemon/src/repository/publication-candidate.ts:21`), so `repository.publish` pushes `master` to `origin`. `release.decide` then opens the PR from the publisher's most recent PUSHED receipt branch (`release-decide-service.ts:85-108`, `pushedBranchOf`) against the operator-typed `base`, which the Release card defaults to "main" (`goal-release.tsx:78`).

On UnAI the remote's default branch is `master` (`git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD` → `refs/heads/master`), so:
1. base "main" names a branch that does not exist on the remote → gh refuses;
2. even with base "master", head == base → no pull request can exist between a branch and itself.

So Release on a trunk-committing workspace can never succeed, and the operator learns it only after Publish, after typing a base, after Approve, as a refusal receipt. The Release card fix a36854f6 explains why Approve is greyed before publish; this task is the flow behind it.

Decide and implement ONE of (the owner's call; state the choice in the plan):
A. Publisher pushes a goal branch (e.g. `moe/release/<goalId>` cut at the landed sha) when the workspace branch equals the remote default branch, and Release opens the PR from that branch. The workspace branch stays untouched.
B. The Release card reads the remote's default branch (daemon measures `symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` or `ls-remote --symref`) and defaults `base` to it, and refuses early with a named code (e.g. RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE) when the publish head equals that base, saying what the operator can do instead.

Either way: the card must never default `base` to a branch the remote does not have.
definitionOfDone: A named refusal (not a gh stderr dump) when the release head equals the base branch, surfaced on the Release card with the branch names.
The Release card's base defaults to the remote's measured default branch, never a hard-coded "main"; a remote without a measurable default leaves the field empty and says so.

A live-shaped test: workspace branch == remote default branch, one landed commit, publish then release → either a PR from a distinct release branch (option A) or the named early refusal (option B); the arm names which option was chosen.
Existing release/publish suites green; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` for src/release/** and src/repository/**, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` for goal-release.
packages/apps CLAUDE.md of the touched folder updated with the rule chosen.

implementationPlan.description: RED then GREEN — the new refusal code. In apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.test.ts first update the pins so they FAIL against today's map: add `RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE` to the exact list at :55 in its sorted position, change the hard-coded `toHaveLength(3)` at :63 to 4, and add a per-code layer assertion beside :44-46 that it maps to `GOAL_PREREQUISITE_LAYER`. Keep the bidirectional set-equality arm at :60-61 exactly as it is — it is what proves the derived roster and the map still agree. Confirm RED. Then in apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.ts add `RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE` to `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODE_LAYER_MAP` with a one-line doc comment in the same register as its neighbours (the daemon's prerequisite read found the pull request's head is its base, so no pull request can exist between them), using the declared layer constant rather than a bare string — a bare layer literal at a refusal site is known to red the TASK-LV security census arms. Update the 'Exactly three keys, closed' doc comment to four. `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODES` derives from the map and needs no edit. Confirm GREEN.

RED then GREEN — the guard (DoD 1). In apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.test.ts first add arms asserting the refusal BY VALUE — exact code `RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE`, exact layer, and a detail containing BOTH branch names — never merely that the release did not succeed: (1) the pushed head equals the requested base, so the release refuses; (2) the pushed head differs from the base, so the guard does not fire; (3) THE MIGRATION CASE the guard exists for: a goal whose PUSHED receipt was written BEFORE task-04160615, with branch `master`, released against base `master`. Assert on the injected PR port that `gh` was NEVER invoked in the refusing arms — the guard must fire before any spawn, or it is only renaming a gh failure. Confirm RED. Then in apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.ts add the check immediately after `pushedBranchOf` resolves the head and BEFORE the PR port is called: if head equals base, throw `domainRefusalOf(releaseRefusal("RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE", <detail>))` in the pattern :162-176 already uses. The detail names both branches and says what to do: re-publish the goal, which now targets `moe/release/<goalId>` for a workspace on the remote's default branch. Compare branch names exactly as git does — case-sensitive. Confirm GREEN, then MUTATION-VERIFY arm (1): back up release-decide-service.ts to %TEMP%/moe-task-4ba1e00a-release-decide-service-<workerId>.ts recording its SHA256 (task id in the path, because seat ids are reused and a seat-only backup can hold the wrong vintage), delete the guard, confirm arm (1) goes RED and quote the line, restore by copying the backup back — never `git checkout --` on this shared tree — and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

Serve the measured default to the card (DoD 2, daemon side). In apps/daemon/src/http/release-evidence-read.ts call task-baefab32's `readRemoteDefaultBranch(store, projectId, remoteUrl)` for the project's bound remote and include `remoteDefaultBranch` in the response WHEN IT IS A STRING, OMITTING the key entirely when it is null — absent means unmeasured, which is what keeps every existing ReleaseEvidenceView fixture valid under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. It is a local store read with no network call, so it is safe on this polled path. In apps/control-room/src/live/live-release.ts add `readonly remoteDefaultBranch?: string` to `ReleaseEvidenceView` (:66) with a one-line doc comment: the default branch the remote itself reported, absent when it has never been measured or could not be. Add arms to apps/daemon/src/http/release-read.test.ts, which is where release-evidence-read's tests already live: a measured default appears by value; an unmeasured one leaves the key ABSENT rather than null — assert with `not.toHaveProperty`, because `toEqual` treats a missing key and an undefined value alike and would pass either way.

The card (DoD 1 and DoD 2, control-room side). In apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-release.tsx replace `useState("main")` (:78) so the card NEVER defaults to a branch the remote does not have. THE REACT TRAP: `useState`'s initializer runs once, and evidence can arrive after first render, so a plain `useState(evidence?.remoteDefaultBranch ?? "")` would capture the pre-load value and never update. Keep a 'touched' flag set when the operator edits the field; until then, derive base from `evidence?.remoteDefaultBranch ?? ""` on every render; after it, the operator's value wins. When no default is measured the field starts EMPTY and the card says so in one plain line near the field — that the remote's default branch is not known yet, so the operator should type the branch to release into. Approve stays disabled while the field is empty, which the existing `trimmed !== ""` guard (:91) already enforces — do not duplicate it. Render a RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE answer with its detail visible, since the detail names both branches and what to do. Arms in apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx, each asserting the rendered field and text by value: a measured default pre-fills base; evidence arriving AFTER first render still pre-fills it (the trap); an operator's edit is NOT overwritten by a later evidence refresh; no measured default leaves the field empty with the explanatory line and Approve disabled; a RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE answer shows both branch names.

THE LIVE-SHAPED ARM (DoD 3) and the docs (DoD 5). (A) In apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.test.ts, drive the whole option-A flow on a real git repository in a temp dir, following the real-repository fixture style the repository tests already use: a workspace whose branch EQUALS the remote's default (create a bare remote whose HEAD symref names `master`, and a workspace on `master` with one landed commit); record the measured default through task-baefab32's production path; publish; then release. Assert by value that publish pushed `refs/heads/moe/release/<goalId>` and did NOT move the bare remote's `master`, that the PUSHED receipt names `moe/release/<goalId>`, and that the release requested a PR with head `moe/release/<goalId>` and base `master` — inject the PR port rather than calling real `gh`. Name in the arm's title that it proves OPTION A, as DoD 3 requires. (B) Update the CLAUDE.md of the touched folder with the rule chosen — apps/daemon/CLAUDE.md unless the release or repository folder carries its own — in its existing register: when a project's workspace branch is the remote's default branch, or that default has not been measured, publish pushes `moe/release/<goalId>` and never the default branch itself; Release opens its PR from that branch into the measured default; and RELEASE_HEAD_IS_BASE is the named refusal when a head and base still coincide, as they do for goals published before this rule.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (DoD 4). (A) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release src/repository src/http/release-read.test.ts`, count line quoted — read the OUTPUT, not the exit code; a leg with no `Test Files N passed` line ran nothing. (B) `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, count line quoted — apps/control-room is in neither the root lane nor the daemon leg, so without this leg a broken card ships behind green gates. (C) The full `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`, both quoted. Attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline rule; re-run a failing daemon file ALONE before attributing it (the full suite throws spurious 5s-timeout reds under parallelism), name which you re-ran, and capture stderr. (D) ADVERSARIAL REVIEW in the completion record: Can the guard be bypassed — differing case, a trailing slash, a `refs/heads/` prefix on one side only? Does it fire before ANY spawn in every path, including the automatic release in release-auto-decide.ts, which reaches the PR port without the card? Can the card still default to `main` anywhere, or to a branch from a previous remote? What does an operator see for a goal published to `master` before task-04160615 — is the path from that refusal to a successful release clear and correct? Does omitting `remoteDefaultBranch` versus sending null matter to any consumer? (E) Record as follow-up comments on this row, not new rows: deleting accumulated `moe/release/*` branches from remotes after their PRs merge; and that this epic now has 63 non-archived rows against the advisory ceiling of 40, which is an epic re-slice signal for a governor or the owner, not something for this row to act on.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-18. The OWNER CHOSE OPTION A (asked twice, confirmed after being told it is ~3 rows). Option A measured ~15+ files, so it is SPLIT in build order and this row is the FINAL of three: task-baefab32f1264daf8f173efc0c1fe2c0 measures and records a remote's default branch as an ADDITIVE event (exporting `readRemoteDefaultBranch(store, projectId, remoteUrl): string | null`); task-0416061566de49939e91bbd6351be79e makes publish push `moe/release/<goalId>` when the workspace branch is the recorded default or the default is unknown. dependsOn on THIS row is [task-baefab32, task-04160615], and task-04160615 itself waits on task-baefab32.

(1) THE DEFECT CHAIN (source reads). publication-candidate.ts:21 takes the workspace's `symbolic-ref HEAD` as the publish branch; git-publication-port.ts:66 pushes `${sha}:refs/heads/${approval.branch}`; release-decide-service.ts:85-108 `pushedBranchOf` takes the last PUSHED receipt's branch as the PR head; goal-release.tsx:78 hard-codes `useState("main")` as base. On UnAI the default is `master`: base `main` does not exist on the remote, and base `master` equals head.

(2) THE REFUSAL VOCABULARY IS DAEMON-LOCAL, SO NO DIGEST ROTATES. `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODE_LAYER_MAP` lives only in apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.ts (`git grep -n "RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING\|RELEASE_PR_FAILED" -- 'packages/**'` returns nothing), documented 'Exactly three keys, closed', with `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODES` DERIVED from its keys. The epic's four-row / digest-mirror rail governs new command KINDS on the shared runtime roster, not a code added to this daemon-local map.

(3) THE PINS ON THAT MAP — all in ONE file, apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.test.ts: per-code layer assertions at :44-46; the EXACT list `expect(RELEASE_DECIDE_CODES).toEqual([...])` at :55; bidirectional set equality at :60-61; a HARD-CODED COUNT `toHaveLength(3)` at :63; an iteration at :69. Control-room tests (offer-wire.test.ts:56-58, live-goal-release.test.tsx:230) use literal codes and hold no copy of the map.

(4) THE LAYER CONSTANT. :45 asserts `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE` maps to `GOAL_PREREQUISITE_LAYER`, a declared constant whose value is "DAEMON_PREREQUISITE". A bare layer literal at a refusal site is known to red the TASK-LV security census arms; use the declared constant.

(5) THE CARD'S DATA PATH. `GoalRelease({ evidence, frame, goalId, port })` (goal-release.tsx:77) receives `evidence: ReleaseEvidenceView` from `LiveGoalRelease` (live-goal-release.tsx:95/:102), which reads apps/daemon/src/http/release-evidence-read.ts. That module's tests live in apps/daemon/src/http/release-read.test.ts (there is NO release-evidence-read.test.ts). `ReleaseEvidenceView` is declared at apps/control-room/src/live/live-release.ts:66 and is NOT decoded with an exact key set (no exactDataRecord / Object.keys / KEYS check in that file), so adding a field cannot red a strict client decoder. Literal fixtures DO construct it (e.g. apps/control-room/src/v2/workspace/product-workspace-state.test.tsx:14), and tsconfig.base sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`.

(6) THE REACT TRAP. `useState("main")` runs its initializer ONCE. Evidence may arrive AFTER first render, so `useState(evidence?.remoteDefaultBranch ?? "")` would capture the pre-load value and never update. The default must re-derive until the operator edits the field.

(7) WHY DoD 1 IS NOT MERELY A THEORETICAL GUARD. Goals UnAI published BEFORE task-04160615 hold PUSHED receipts whose branch is `master`. Once the card defaults base to the measured default (`master`), releasing one of those goals gives head == base. The guard turns that from an opaque `gh` stderr dump into a named refusal that tells the operator to re-publish — which, under task-04160615's rule, now targets `moe/release/<goalId>`. That is the migration path for the owner's in-flight goals.
